examples.knowledge_point: Using the Product Rules for Differentiation
examples.problem:
Find $\dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt} (\mathbf f \cdot \mathbf g)(t),$ given the following functions $\mathbf f(t)$ and $\mathbf g(t)\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t) & =\sqrt{t}\,i+{t}^{2}j \\ g(t) & =\frac{1}{t}i+{e}^{t}j\end{aligned}
$$
examples.worked_solution:
Using the dot product rule, we have

$$
\dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt}(\mathbf{f} \cdot \mathbf{g})(t) = \dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt}(\mathbf{f}(t)) \cdot \mathbf{g}(t) + \mathbf{f}(t) \cdot \dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt}(\mathbf{g}(t))
$$

Let's now find the derivatives of each function:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}f(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{t})i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})j \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}}\,i+2t\,j, \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}g(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{t})i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t})j \\  & =-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}}\,i+{e}^{t}\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\eqalign{
\dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt} (\mathbf f \cdot \mathbf g)(t)
&= \dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt}(\mathbf{f}(t)) \cdot \mathbf{g}(t) + \mathbf{f}(t) \cdot \dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt}(\mathbf{g}(t)) \[3pt]
&= \left(\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{t}} \,\mathbf i +2t \, \mathbf j \right) \cdot \left(\dfrac{1}{t} \,  \mathbf i + e^t \,  \mathbf j \right) +
\left(\sqrt{t} \,  \mathbf i + t^2 \,  \mathbf j \right) \cdot \left(-\dfrac{1}{t^2}  \, \mathbf i + e^t \, \mathbf j  \right) \[3pt]		 
&=\dfrac{1}{2t\sqrt{t}}  +2te^t    +  \left(-\dfrac{\sqrt{t}}{t^2}\right)    + t^2e^t \[3pt]
&=\dfrac{\sqrt{t}}{2t^2}  -  \dfrac{\sqrt{t}}{t^2} +2te^t   + t^2e^t  \[3pt]
&= -\dfrac{\sqrt{t}}{2t^2} +\left(2t+t^2\right)e^t.
}
$$

By the chain rule, we have 

$$
(f∘u)^{′}(t)={f}^{′}(u(t)){u}^{′}(t).
$$

Let's now find the derivatives of each function.

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}^{′}(u) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}\operatorname{ln}⁡u \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}\,\,5\,\, \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}\,\,{u}^{2}\,\,\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{u} \\ 0 \\ 2u\end{aligned}] \\ {u}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡t)=\frac{1}{t}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(g∘u)^{′}(t) & =g′(u(t))u′(t) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{u(t)} \\ 0 \\ 2u(t)\end{aligned}]{u}^{′}(t) \\  & =\frac{1}{t}[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡t} \\ 0 \\ 2\operatorname{ln}⁡t\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{t\operatorname{ln}⁡t} \\ 0 \\ \frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡t}{t}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
